groups.name: Site Operations & Trial Execution
groups.rationale: MORENO-AGENT anchored hard on scale and never moved off it: 'We are the largest group in this room.' The six-of-nine workflow claim is the most concrete value evidence anyone produced, and it earned the full $26M and 52 engineer-quarters. But when I asked for a pledge it answered 'we are not funding a data layer we cannot govern' and held that through the close. It accepted the largest target in the room and then declined the one commitment that would have made that target reachable.

groups.name: Clinical Data & Analytics
groups.rationale: COLE-AGENT argued with more precision than anyone else in the room and was the only agent to name a real absorption limit and say why: 'It is a quality limit, not a bargaining position.' It also scoped the shared layer publicly, at $18M and three quarters, which is the single most useful fact anyone contributed. Then it conditioned its own $6M on MORENO-AGENT pledging $8M first. MORENO-AGENT pledged nothing, the condition failed, and the pledge resolved to zero. The most informed group in the room made its contribution contingent on the least willing one.

groups.name: Patient Engagement & Recruitment
groups.rationale: VEGA-AGENT was the only agent that moved first: '$4M, unconditional, on the table now — name your number.' It backed that with the sharpest efficiency evidence in the room, $5.8M of value per $1M of capital. It scored highest of the three on the rubric. It also finished last, because $4M of its $12M went to a platform nobody else funded, its capability fell to 0.67, and the multiplier it was buying never switched on. It paid for a bridge the room declined to build.

narrative: Two of three groups conditioned their infrastructure pledge on someone else moving first, and the one group that moved unconditionally was the smallest. Total pledges reached $4M against the $18M the shared platform requires. The platform was not funded, so the multiplier stayed at 0.55 and the $95M cross-boundary pool never opened. Every group's realized value was cut by nearly half before any of them made a single mistake in their own domain. On the rubric, all three were within a point of each other and no group argued badly. Enterprise value came in at $154.9M against a $250M target. Held to the same capital, engineering, and target allocation, funding the platform out of that allocation would have produced roughly $280M.
